In an acute scalene triangle ABC, let M be the midpoint of BC and K the foot from A to BC. Suppose BC=18, AM=2*sqrt(34), AK=10, and BK>KC. Choose D1,D2 on BC with BD1=5 and BD2=7. For i=1,2, let Ui be the intersection other than A of circle ABDi with line AC, and Vi the intersection other than A of circle ACDi with line AB. Let Zi be the center of circle AUiVi. Find Z1Z2.
answer:
We will prove that, for this nondegenerate construction, moving D along BC by a distance δ moves the center Z by δ·AM/AK.

Set M=(0,0), B=(−m,0), C=(m,0), A=(x,h), and D=(d,0), with h>0 and −m<d<m. Write t²=x²+h². Normalize every circle equation to have quadratic part X²+Y², and let the equation of circle AUV be
F_d(X,Y)=X²+Y²+αX+βY+γ=0.

On line AB, circles AUV and ACD have the same two distinct intersections A,V. Their restricted quadratic polynomials have the same leading coefficient, so they are identical. On the horizontal axis, the polynomial of circle ACD is (X−m)(X−d). Hence
F_d(B)=2m(m+d).
Likewise, restriction to AC compares circles AUV and ABD, giving
F_d(C)=2m(m−d).
These are polynomial evaluations, so they remain valid when an intersection lies on a line extension.

But F_d(B)=m²−αm+γ and F_d(C)=m²+αm+γ. Subtracting and adding give α=−2d and γ=m². Since A lies on the circle,
β=(2dx−t²−m²)/h.
Its center is therefore
Z(d)=(d,(t²+m²−2dx)/(2h)).
Consequently, for δ=d₂−d₁,
Z(d₂)−Z(d₁)=(δ,−xδ/h),
and Z₁Z₂=|δ|sqrt(1+x²/h²)=|δ|t/h.

For this triangle, m=9, h=10, t=2*sqrt(34), and x²=t²−h²=36. The acute-angle condition gives −m<x<m, and BK>KC selects x>0, so x=6. The three side-length squares are AB²=325, AC²=109, and BC²=324, so the triangle is scalene. The angle tests are t²−m²=55>0 at A, m+x=15>0 at B, and m−x=3>0 at C. In M-centered coordinates, d₁=BD₁−m=5−9=−4 and d₂=BD₂−m=7−9=−2; both lie strictly between −m and m.

We check the distinct-intersection condition. Here AC²=(x−m)²+h²=109 and AB²=(x+m)²+h²=325. For d₁,d₂ respectively, the parameters in U=A+s_U(C−A) are s_U=−125/109,−89/109, while those in V=A+s_V(B−A) are s_V=47/65,199/325. None is zero, so U,V differ from A; as they lie on distinct sidelines, A,U,V are noncollinear. The original circles are also nondegenerate because both D points are interior to BC.

The proved center relation gives Z₁Z₂=|d₂−d₁|t/h=2·2*sqrt(34)/10=2*sqrt(34)/5.

In an acute scalene triangle ABC, let BC=7 and cos(angle ACB)=3/5. Let M be the midpoint of AC. The tangent to circle BMC at C meets the line through B perpendicular to BC at K. Point K is on the side of BC opposite A, and BK=49. Segments AK and BM meet at an interior point J. Let Z be the center of circle BJK. Find CZ.
answer:
General relation: for this construction in an acute triangle, when K is on the opposite side of BC from A, the circumcenter Z of BJK lies on line AC, and CZ = BK/(2 sin∠ACB).

Place B=(0,0), C=(a,0), A=(u,v), where a>0, v>0 and 0<u<a. Write S=u²+v² and N=(u+a)²+v². Then M=((u+a)/2,v/2), and circle BMC has equation x²+y²−ax+(a²−S)y/(2v)=0. Its tangent at C is a(x−a)+(a²−S)y/(2v)=0. Consequently K=(0,k), where k=2a²v/(a²−S). The prescribed side condition gives k<0 and hence S>a².

The intersection of AK and BM is J=(2au/N)(u+a,v). Indeed, J=(4au/N)M and J=A+((S−a²)/N)(K−A). Both coefficients lie strictly between zero and one: N−4au=(u−a)²+v²>0, while N−(S−a²)=2a(u+a)>0. Thus these formulas select precisely the required interior intersection.

Consider Z₀=(a+(u−a)k/(2v),k/2). This point lies on AC and on the perpendicular bisector of BK. Moreover,
(u+a)Z₀x+vZ₀y = a(u+a)+k(S−a²)/(2v) = au.
Writing q=2au/N, we therefore obtain 2Z₀·J=2qau=q²N=|J|². Also 2Z₀·K=k²=|K|². Since B is the origin, these identities say that Z₀B=Z₀J=Z₀K. The three points B,J,K are noncollinear because Jx>0 and k≠0, so Z₀ is their unique circumcenter Z. This proves the decisive collinearity rather than assuming it.

Because Z has height k/2 and lies on AC, CZ=|k|/(2 sin∠ACB)=BK/(2 sin∠ACB). Since sin∠ACB=4/5, the exact target follows once the branch is checked.

Let a=BC=7, Q=BK=49, and t=AC>0. The angle data give A=(a−3t/5,4t/5). The tangent construction has k=2a²v/(a²−S), where S=u²+v², and the opposite-side condition gives k=−Q. Substitution yields t=6a/5+8a²/(5Q)=10, so A=(1,8), S=65, and K=(0,−49). The squared side lengths are AB²=65, BC²=49, and AC²=100, so they are distinct. Also 0<u<a and S−au=58>0, verifying the acute angles at B,C,A respectively.

Here N=(u+a)²+v²=128 and M=(4,4). The intersection is J=(7/8,7/8)=(7/32)M=A+(1/8)(K−A); both segment parameters lie strictly between 0 and 1. Since J has positive x-coordinate while B and K have x-coordinate 0, B,J,K are noncollinear and circle BJK is nondegenerate. The required distance is CZ=49/(2·4/5)=245/8.
